races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Thai Ginger
runners_data.comment: February foal; 100,000gns yearling; first foal from 2021 Queen Mary Stks winner Quick Suzy
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 100,000gns yearling; first foal from the 2021 Queen Mary Stakes winner Quick Suzy (RPR 106); stable is yet to really get going with juveniles this year but has operated at a 12% strike-rate (24-196) over the last five years; notable candidate.

runners_data.name: Thunda Struck
runners_data.comment: April foal; 16,000euros yearling; second foal from a 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 96).
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 16,000euros yearling; second foal from a 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 96), who was a half-sister to two winners (7.5f-1m4f); trainer is 0-1 with his juveniles this year; let the market guide.

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.comment: Showed speed before weakening on recent Beverley debut (5f, fillies' maiden; 12-1).
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; dam was a 5f winner (RPR 94); showed speed before weakening on recent Beverley debut (5f, fillies' maiden; 12-1, seventh of 11); that race run in a marginally slower time than division 1 - contested by Bluestone Lady - earlier in the afternoon.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.comment: Only eighth of 11 at Beverley (5f, fillies' novice; 9-2) ten days ago; could do better.
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; half-sister to two winners (6f-8.6f); never better than midfield, eighth of 11 to the promising Princesse d'Orange at Beverley (5f, fillies' novice, good to soft; 9-2) ten days ago; is in capable hands though, so could do better with that experience banked.

runners_data.name: Bettabebougie
runners_data.comment: Hung left-handed when last of four on recent Southwell debut (5f, novice; 10-1; btn 14l+).
runners_data.spotlight: April foal, and a half sister to a 1m1f Czech winner; hung left-handed when last of four on recent Southwell debut (5f, novice; 10-1; beaten over 14l); will need to improve markedly on that opening AW effort to stake a realistic claim.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Triumph
runners_data.note: Highly-bred newcomer with excellent pedigree but unknown running style making debut assessment difficult
runners_data.comment: Good pedigree and a threat to all if the betting speaks in her favour
runners_data.spotlight: Good pedigree, being a half-sister to seven winners, including Sheraz (1m3f-1m7f including Listed; RPR 116), Lakota Sioux (7f 2yo including Group 3; 100), Shehiyr (9.5f-1m4f including AW; 99) and Surrey Gold (8.6f-1m6f; 98); dam 1m2f Group 3 winner; doesn't have that high a standard to aim at and market confidence would look significant.

runners_data.name: Always Blue
runners_data.note: Sister to Swedish winner trained by in-form Harriet Bethell but market movements will be crucial indicator
runners_data.comment: In good hands but best watched this time unless the betting hints otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: By Masar and a sister to a 1m winner in Sweden; in good hands but a watching brief is advised this time unless the betting hints otherwise.

runners_data.name: Romance Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who needs strong pace but encouraging debut second suggests step up in trip will suit
runners_data.comment: Promising second on 1m debut; this trip should suit better; the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: Teofilo filly who made an encouraging start to her career when second of five on 1m Southwell debut (Tapeta) 23 days ago, keeping on as if this longer trip is sure to suit; leading claims with improvement likely.

runners_data.name: Miss Malone To You
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with stamina pedigree but concerning finish-fade tendency and long 143-day layoff
runners_data.comment: Only eighth on 1m debut but this half-sister to Big Orange has potential for longer trips
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to connections' top stayer Big Orange and several other winners; 28-1, 5l eighth of 12 on 1m Lingfield debut in December; has the potential for better over longer trips in 2026.

runners_data.name: Mudita
runners_data.note: Showed promise on Wolverhampton debut and step up to 1m2f should suit but needs to find significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Some promise amid inexperience when third on 7f debut; up in trip; likely to improve
runners_data.spotlight: Showed a bit of promise amid inexperience when 5.75l third of eight on 7f Wolverhampton debut in March; didn't achieve a great deal but is likely to improve up nearly 3f in trip.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Skye
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner in field but modest form for previous trainer and new stable has poor strike rate
runners_data.comment: Modest form when placed three times for Alice Haynes last year; more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form when finishing third on three of her four starts at up to an extended 1m for Alice Haynes last year; improvement will be needed starting out for a new yard after five months off.

races.paceDynamic: Exquisite Skye will likely take the field along from the front with no obvious pace pressure in this small field of six maidens. The lack of natural speed horses means she can dictate comfortable fractions through the early stages at 1m2f on good ground. Romance Spirit, Mudita and Miss Malone To You are all hold-up types who will need the pace to develop, while the two newcomers Triumph and Always Blue have unknown running styles but pedigrees suggesting middle-distance ability. This race setup strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed, as the lack of genuine pace will make it difficult for hold-up horses to find the strong gallop they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Skye gets an easy lead and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: She can control the tempo completely and have enough left to resist late challenges on the long Ripon straight. The lack of early pace pressure allows her to save energy for when the hold-up horses come with their runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Newcomer Shows Class
scenarios.trigger: If either Triumph or Always Blue shows natural ability and tactical awareness on debut
scenarios.body: Their higher ratings and superior pedigrees could prove decisive if they adapt quickly to racing. Triumph's half-sister connections to multiple winners including Listed performer Sheraz suggests significant untapped potential.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong despite appearances and sets up perfectly for closers
scenarios.body: Romance Spirit's encouraging debut second would make her the most likely beneficiary of a truly-run race. Her Teofilo breeding and step up in trip from 1m debut suggests she has more to offer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Exquisite Skye goes too slowly early then multiple horses challenge simultaneously in final furlong
scenarios.body: The lack of a strong pace could see several horses with chances turning for home creating a messy finish. This unpredictable scenario could suit any horse with a turn of foot regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: Watch Exquisite Skye's early fractions as she's the only pace angle and could steal this if uncontested
Monitor betting movements on newcomers Triumph and Always Blue as their pedigrees suggest significant ability
Romance Spirit needs genuine pace development but Hollie Doyle booking suggests connections expect improvement
Miss Malone To You's 143-day break and previous fading tendency makes her vulnerable despite Big Orange connections
Track any late jockey changes as several trainers have moderate recent strike rates

races.name: Visit attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: Hold-up stayer with Newcastle wins but handicapper has caught up since, needs strong pace to set up his finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Two wins at Newcastle at the start of the year but handicapper in charge since
runners_data.spotlight: Out-and-out stayer who won twice at Newcastle (2m, Tapeta) at the start of the year but the handicapper has been winning the argument since; it remains to be seen whether a return to turf makes any difference in that regard.

runners_data.name: Diamand De Vindecy
runners_data.note: Returns from hurdling with fitness advantage, showed best form in April last year including course second
runners_data.comment: Fit from hurdling and feasibly treated on last April's Flat form
runners_data.spotlight: Arrives fit from hurdling and some of his best Flat form last year came in April, winning at Pontefract before second over C&D (both good).

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Front runner coming off impressive Bath win, 5lb claimer offsets penalty, gets tactical advantage as likely lone leader
runners_data.comment: Ready win at Bath last week and 4lb rise if offset by rider's claim; can follow up
runners_data.spotlight: Ready winner back from a break at Bath (2m1f, good to firm) eight days ago; his 4lb rise is offset by Mason Paetel's claim; likely to follow up.

runners_data.name: Zimmerman
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from long break, has been placed twice at course and distance previously
runners_data.comment: Drew a blank in 2025 but did reach the frame on both C&D visits; off for 196 days
runners_data.spotlight: Drew a blank in 2025 but he did reach the frame on both C&D visits, including C&D reappearance; off for 196 days; David Allan partners the other Tim Easterby runner.

runners_data.name: Rupert The Prince
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner with three wins from last five starts, switches from Paddy Butler to Rebecca Menzies
runners_data.comment: Well held on hurdle debut for new yard but progressive on Flat last year
runners_data.spotlight: Won three of his last five Flat runs for Paddy Butler, including a clearcut success at Bath (2m1f, soft) in October; no impact on hurdle debut for new yard in January but could fare a lot better back on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Unexposed 4yo stepping up markedly in trip, David Allan booking suggests confidence from in-form Easterby yard
runners_data.comment: Never involved on recent 1m4f handicap debut but remains unexposed now up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who was never involved on his recent 1m4f Pontefract handicap debut but did show some promise in his qualifying runs; up 4f in trip now.

runners_data.name: Stitching Wheel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who hasn't fired since arriving from France, needs significant improvement at bottom of weights
runners_data.comment: Displayed early promise on Flat in France but hasn't shown much in Britain; tongue tied
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed early promise on the Flat in France but hasn't shown much since coming to Britain, including back on the Flat at Catterick (1m4f) 17 days ago; up markedly in trip now with a tongue-tie added.

races.paceDynamic: No More Bolero will take the field along as the sole confirmed front runner, with Zimmerman, Rupert The Prince and possibly the handicap debutant Treasure Islands settling prominently behind. The pace should be sustainable rather than breakneck given the lack of early pace pressure on No More Bolero over this staying trip. The hold-up horses Tarbat Ness, Diamand De Vindecy and Stitching Wheel will need the leaders to come back to them in the final three furlongs. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and the pace-setter who can dictate fractions without interference.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero gets an easy lead without early pressure
scenarios.body: The recent Bath winner can dictate comfortable fractions and has too much in hand when the challenges come. His 4lb penalty is negated by the 5lb claim and tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Zimmerman or Rupert The Prince press No More Bolero early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more honest, setting up a battle between the prominent racers in the straight. Rupert The Prince's class from his Bath wins could tell.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the leaders tire
scenarios.body: Tarbat Ness or Diamand De Vindecy can time their runs to perfection as the front rank weakens. The Newcastle winner Tarbat Ness has the strongest staying form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Treasure Islands Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the Tim Easterby 4yo takes to the extended trip immediately
scenarios.body: The unexposed handicap debutant shows significant improvement stepping up 4f in distance. David Allan's booking and stable form support this theory.

watchPoints.text: No More Bolero getting loose on the lead - if uncontested through halfway he may prove unstoppable
How Zimmerman handles his first run in 196 days - fitness versus class equation for the Tim Easterby runner
Treasure Islands taking to the extended trip - if traveling well turning in he could outrun odds as unexposed type
The pace through the middle sections - genuine gallop needed to bring hold-up horses Tarbat Ness and Diamand De Vindecy into play
Rupert The Prince adapting to new connections - three wins from five starts suggests he's a consistent performer ready to fire

races.name: M.C.H. Hutchinson Memorial Trophy Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prydwen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to lead early but recent AW form raises questions about his turf effectiveness after 168 days off the surface
runners_data.comment: Good second in a warm race on AW over Easter and should go well back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Last five outings on AW, posting his most encouraging effort when second of 12 in a 2m Newcastle Good Friday handicap; nudged back up 2lb for that but he's still 3lb lower than when runner-up at Chester (2m, good to soft) last September; should go well.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse returning from a 168-day break but David O'Meara's 5/28 form is solid and horse has won fresh before
runners_data.comment: Smart handicapper who ran several good races last year; has gone well fresh before
runners_data.spotlight: Smart handicapper who won at Haydock (1m4f, good) off 4lb lower last May and recorded several good efforts in defeat later in 2025; has gone well fresh before.

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace scenario and his Goodwood success over this trip on good ground is a strong pointer
runners_data.comment: Dual winner for Ralph Beckett; new yard runs three and the betting may guide
runners_data.spotlight: Second career success when shading a tight finish at Goodwood (1m4f, good to firm) last August; ended the year with a poor run at Newcastle (1m4f) in September; subsequently sold out of Ralph Beckett's stable for 30,000gns; new yard runs three and the betting is perhaps the best guide to expectations.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: French import making only second British start for in-form David O'Meara yard, prominent style could see him involved early
runners_data.comment: Pretty useful in France but no obvious short-term encouragement on yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Pretty useful at up to 1m4f in France but only eighth of 12 in 1m2f Doncaster handicap on British debut four weeks ago; the type to click for this yard at some point but possibly a bit further down the line.

runners_data.name: Dancingwithmyself
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who was second in this very race last year and has since improved with two wins over longer trips
runners_data.comment: Fine second on reappearance and Ripon form figures are 112; leading claims
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in this race (good) on her 2025 reappearance and went on to score twice at about 1m6f later in the year; returned with a career-best second of 13 at Musselburgh (1m6f, soft) three weeks ago, arguably deserving extra credit considering she met a bit of trouble; successful on her two other visits to Ripon; reasons to be positive.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Deep closer who needs a strong pace but his course and distance record of 2-3 gives him a significant tactical edge
runners_data.comment: Hard to derive much encouragement from recent reappearance but he is 2-3 over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground winner over this trip at Catterick last autumn; hard to derive much encouragement from his recent Thirsk reappearance but the fact he's 2-3 over C&D (all 2022) provides some hope.

races.paceDynamic: Prydwen and Prince Of The Seas will likely dispute early leadership, with Ashnak also showing prominent tendencies to press the pace. The hold-up quartet of Stressfree, Dancingwithmyself and Gibside will need the leaders to go hard enough to come back to them in the final 2f. With multiple prominent runners likely to commit early over this staying trip, the pace should be solid and sustainable rather than crawling. This race shape clearly favours the hold-up horses who can capitalize on a decent gallop and time their runs from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Prydwen and Prince Of The Seas set a solid early pace with Ashnak pressing
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for the closers, with Stressfree and Dancingwithmyself having ideal conditions to unleash late runs. The early leaders will have done too much work over the extended trip to resist the finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes moderate with the leaders allowed to coast
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners can dictate terms and have enough left for the finish, particularly if the hold-up horses find insufficient pace to aim at. Prince Of The Seas or Ashnak could capitalize on tactical speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all prominent runners go too hard early and tie up badly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a war of attrition where only the deepest closers survive, with Gibside's stamina reserves potentially proving decisive. The hold-up horses will have a field day picking up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Prydwen gets an uncontested lead and the field allows him soft fractions
scenarios.body: Without sufficient early pressure, Prydwen could steal a march and hold on grimly, particularly given his recent form improvement. The hold-up horses would be caught flat-footed by the lack of pace.

watchPoints.text: Stressfree could be vulnerable to the layoff despite previous fresh form, as 168 days is a significant absence for any handicapper
Watch Ashnak's early positioning as his prominent style could see him drawn into a pace battle he cannot sustain on only his second British start
Prince Of The Seas needs monitoring for early pace involvement as his prominent style could either set him up perfectly or leave him exposed
Prydwen's effectiveness returning to turf after five consecutive AW runs is questionable despite his recent form improvement
The hold-up trio of Stressfree, Dancingwithmyself and Gibside will need the early pace to be honest to have optimal winning chances

races.name: Ripon Silver Sprint Trophy Handicap

runners_data.name: Seven Questions
runners_data.note: Prominent runner gets likely uncontested lead with Hollie Doyle up, dropping to reduced mark after long losing spell
runners_data.comment: Drawn a blank since 2024 Group 3 success but reappearance third quite encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Losing spell goes back to his Palace House success two years ago but he has a reduced mark to work with as a result and he ran well when third on his Pontefract reappearance (5f, good to soft) 18 days ago; player if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 187 days off, fading tendency but well-treated mark after blank 2025 season
runners_data.comment: Multiple winner who is on a good mark on return for new trainer; betting informative
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-time winner down the years for James Evans; drew a blank in 2025 but runner-up twice off marks in the 90s, including reappearance, so well treated starting out for Tony Carroll (same owners); interesting to see what the betting makes of him.

runners_data.name: Dyonisos
runners_data.note: Hold-up type showed best British form when second at Newmarket 11 days ago, handles good ground well
runners_data.comment: Encouraging return to Britain at Newmarket last week; bold show likely from same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time winner over 6f in France who ran his best race in Britain when second of eight to same owner's Jakajaro at Newmarket (5f, good to soft) 11 days ago; bold show likely from an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Copper Knight
runners_data.note: 12-year-old veteran in prominent style, never won at Ripon but three 5f wins last year prove he retains ability
runners_data.comment: This 12yo added three more wins last year but has yet to win first time out
runners_data.spotlight: None of today's opponents were foaled when he won his first race but this 12yo was still pretty useful last year, winning three times over 5f; the fact he's never won first time up suggests it may pay to look elsewhere this time, though.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Prominent runner coming off 5f win at Southwell 18 days ago, yet to succeed above mark of 76 so faces career-best requirement
runners_data.comment: Won at Southwell this month but career best needed to follow up off 6lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Placed three times on AW over the winter before resuming winning ways over 5f at Southwell 18 days ago; hasn't been successful above a mark of 76 so a career best will be needed if he's to follow up.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Prominent style, encouraging return when sixth at Musselburgh 13 days ago behind stablemate Vince L'Amour
runners_data.comment: Recent reappearance sixth of 17 quite encouraging and only 1lb above his last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Reopposing stablemate Vince L'Amour was ahead in second when sixth of 17 at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) 13 days ago but it was still quite an encouraging return to action from this 5yo who has dipped to only 1lb above the mark he defied at Catterick (5f, good) last September.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 196 days off, won twice over course and distance last year when visor added
runners_data.comment: C&D win last summer but might be best watched minus usual headgear after 196 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Improved when visor was added to her tongue-tie last year, winning over C&D (good) and at Newmarket (good to firm) in August; starts this campaign 5lb above the mark she defied at Newmarket and might be best watched after 196 days off with both the visor and tongue-tie missing.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner improved dramatically to finish second at Musselburgh 13 days ago, racing off just 1lb higher mark
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on reappearance when second in competitive race at Musselburgh latest
runners_data.spotlight: Took a good step forward from his reappearance when second (Equity Law sixth) of 17 at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) 13 days ago; respected off only 1lb higher.

races.paceDynamic: Seven Questions looks the lone natural pace-setter with his prominent style, likely to get an uncontested lead from the rail. The majority of this field prefers to settle - Dream Composer, Dyonisos, Tiva and Vince L'Amour all hold up, while Copper Knight, Castan and Equity Law sit prominent but won't force the issue early. With minimal early pressure, Seven Questions can dictate comfortable fractions before the hold-up horses launch their challenges in the final furlong. This race shape clearly favours the front-runner who gets first run, plus any pace-presser like Copper Knight or Castan who can track the leader without getting involved in early speed duels.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Seven Questions gets away cleanly and faces no early pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: The Hollie Doyle-ridden favourite can control the tempo completely and prove hard to peg back when the hold-up horses make their moves. His reduced mark and recent Pontefract third suggest he retains enough ability to capitalise on ideal conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and Seven Questions kicks too late
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash devastating late runs in a slowly-run race. Dyonisos showed his best British form when second at Newmarket and could time his challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Pressure Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Copper Knight or Castan decide to challenge Seven Questions early
scenarios.body: Any pace battle up front will set up the race for the deeper closers who can pick up the pieces. The 12-year-old Copper Knight might not have the stamina for a speed duel over this minimum trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Seven Questions sets steady fractions but one of the prominent runners gets the perfect tracking position
scenarios.body: A horse like Castan or Equity Law could get the best of both worlds - avoiding early pace pressure while staying close enough to strike. Castan's recent Southwell win suggests he's in good heart.

watchPoints.text: Seven Questions must break cleanly from the rail to establish his crucial early position without interference
Copper Knight's stamina at 12 years old if he gets involved in any early pace pressure with Seven Questions
Dream Composer's fitness after 187 days off and whether his known fading tendency resurfaces in the finish
Dyonisos following up his Newmarket second if the pace becomes slow enough for his held-up style to be effective
Castan handling the step up in class to a mark of 80 having never won above 76 in his career

races.name: Sue's 60th Birthday Occasion Handicap

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who thrives when there's pace to aim at, returns to scene of last turf win but workable absence of 28 days
runners_data.comment: Third at Wolverhampton (8.5f; 10-1) penultimate; backward step at Doncaster (1m2f) since.
runners_data.spotlight: Last turf win was here (1m2f, good to soft; from 6lb higher) in June 2024; fair third at Wolverhampton (8.5f; 10-1) on penultimate start but took a backward step at Doncaster (1m2f) subsequently; easing mark isn't enough to tempt.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: 11-year-old veteran with prominent style, consistent form on similar going and proven at the course
runners_data.comment: Veteran (12-121); seventh last year; should strip fitter for Pontefract (1m) comeback run.
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran (12-121); seventh (beaten 4l; 40-1) in this last year; broadly consistent since accounting for Ravishing Beauty at Carlisle (1m, soft; similar terms) last September; should strip fitter for recent Pontefract (1m; fourth of nine; 33-1) comeback run.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Front-runner in excellent form after last week's all-the-way win, faces 3lb rise but quick turnaround of 7 days
runners_data.comment: Showed a willing attitude to make all at Nottingham (8.5f, good) last Saturday; 3lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Built on Wolverhampton comeback run (7f) when showing a willing attitude to make all at Nottingham (8.5f, good) last Saturday; 3lb rise isn't insurmountable but he is set to compete from a career-high mark, so further progress is required.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who remains a maiden despite multiple places, 5lb claiming jockey takes pressure off
runners_data.comment: 0-14; ran respectably when fourth in a newly applied visor at Catterick (7f, good) latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden (0-14), runner-up five times, including in a 6f Southwell novice last November; ran respectably (keen) when fourth in a newly applied visor at Catterick (7f, good) latest; should stay a mile (first go) and is on a fair mark, more so if factoring in Mason Paetel's 5lb claim.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form came in summer 2023, trainer out of form recently with 0/23 record
runners_data.comment: Won at Doncaster (1m) & Musselburgh (1m1f) last August; ninth of 13 at Thirsk (1m) latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Won back-to-back at Doncaster (1m) and Musselburgh (1m1f) last August, running down Drumcondra latterly; held off higher marks since, including when ninth of 13 at Thirsk (1m, good; beaten nearly 6l) latest; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is helpful.

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 192-day break, previously too keen when tried in a visor over course and distance
runners_data.comment: Won from 7lb lower at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) in September; potentially vulnerable.
runners_data.spotlight: Lit up by a visor (too keen) when a weakening third over C&D last June; did manage to win twice thereafter (with headgear discarded), including from 7lb lower at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) in September; potentially vulnerable off a 192-day absence.

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty
runners_data.note: Closer who showed good form last summer, long absence of 193 days is a concern despite past course success
runners_data.comment: Won twice last summer (8f-8.5f); runner-up to Poet's Dawn at Carlisle (1m) in September.
runners_data.spotlight: In fine fettle last summer, winning at Pontefract (1m) and Nottingham (8.5f); found Poet's Dawn too strong at Carlisle (1m, soft; similar terms) in September; off since finishing third at Newcastle in October, so may strip fitter for this comeback run.

runners_data.name: Currumbin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner better known for longer distances and hurdles, recent comeback at Yarmouth was disappointing
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on recent Yarmouth comeback (1m2f); hasn't run over a mile since late 2024.
runners_data.spotlight: Both Flat wins came on AW (1m6f-2m); relatively quiet since winning over hurdles at Worcester (2m, maiden) last June; well beaten on recent Yarmouth comeback (1m2f), and he hasn't run over a mile since late 2024; others preferred.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Front-runner who just got off the mark last time, faces 3lb rise and has Hollie Doyle taking the ride
runners_data.comment: Off the mark at the 13th attempt at Nottingham (8.5f, good) latest; now 3lb higher.
runners_data.spotlight: Dropped back in trip when getting off the mark at the 13th attempt at Nottingham (8.5f, good) latest; the winning margin there was just a nose but, with a 3lb rise, he remains on a reasonably competitive mark; Hollie Doyle is back aboard.

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won last time out but reportedly ran too freely when disappointing subsequently
runners_data.comment: Sits 2lb above last winning mark; fourth in a Class 4 at Southwell (40-1) latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Resumed winning ways at Beverley (8.5f, soft; from 2lb lower) last September but reportedly ran too freely when soundly beaten at Nottingham next time; caught the eye when fourth in a Class 4 at Southwell (1m; 40-1) recently, but it mightn't be wise to take that form literally.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 304-day layoff with tendency to fade in the finish, longest absence in field
runners_data.comment: Disappointing efforts handicapping (7f-1m); easing mark for return from ten-month absence.
runners_data.spotlight: Rallied to win a modest maiden at Ayr (1m, good; 11-2) last April; disappointing since introduced to handicapping, scarcely managing to beat a rival in three attempts (7f-1m); an easing mark could aid her cause on return from ten-month absence; stablemate of Poet's Dawn.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly and The Sweet Escape are both confirmed front-runners who will dispute the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the outset. With two keen pace-setters likely to go at it early, this sets up a scenario where the tempo will be solid rather than crawling, particularly over this straight mile at Ripon. The pace battle between these two will stretch the field and create opportunities for horses that can quicken from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and closers who can benefit from the early pace injection.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly and The Sweet Escape engage in a sustained pace battle through the first half-mile
scenarios.body: The early leaders compromise each other's finishing kicks, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past in the final furlong with superior finishing speed. Up The Jazz, Amidst The Chaos, and Ravishing Beauty are perfectly positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacemaker Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly or The Sweet Escape gets an uncontested lead while the other fades early
scenarios.body: The surviving front-runner dictates terms and potentially has enough left to resist late challengers, particularly if Highland Olly's recent winning momentum carries forward. The pace becomes more tactical, reducing the closers' advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is only moderate due to tactical riding from the front-runners
scenarios.body: Horses like Poet's Dawn and Hostility, racing prominently, can track the leaders without being stretched and have first run on the weakening pace-setters. This scenario negates the closers' main weapon of a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both Highland Olly and The Sweet Escape are restrained early, creating a crawling pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair that turns into a sprint finish, potentially suiting any horse with a sharp turn of foot regardless of usual running style. The lack of pace makes it a lottery.

watchPoints.text: Highland Olly and The Sweet Escape must be monitored for how aggressively they dispute the early lead as it will determine the entire race shape
Up The Jazz needs to be positioned close enough to benefit from the expected strong pace without getting caught too far back
Keats House faces a significant test returning from 192 days off, watch for any signs of rustiness or over-keen tendencies that plagued previous course runs
Poet's Dawn at 11 years old may struggle if the pace becomes truly searching, despite his consistency
The 5lb claiming riders on Hostility and Amidst The Chaos could prove crucial if the race becomes competitive

runners_data.name: Blue Nguru
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner returning after 129 days off, likely to be keen early with Hollie Doyle aboard
runners_data.comment: Off the mark at Lingfield (5f novice) in December; retains potential off four-month break.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up at Hamilton and Catterick (6f fillies' maiden; first-time cheekpieces) prior to being slowly away at Lingfield (7f) in early December; took her chance - always handy - back there (5f novice) a fortnight later, and has been given a four-month break since; retains potential.

runners_data.name: Arishka's Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good form with narrow defeats lately, sits 2lb high but RPR suggests further improvement
runners_data.comment: 6f Wolverhampton maiden winner; twice narrowly beaten since; merits respect on turf debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Made the breakthrough at Wolverhampton (6f, maiden; 4-1) in February; has bettered that since (on RPRs) with narrow defeats at Lingfield and Newcastle; 2lb higher again, but possible he can stake a claim if proving as effective on turf (debut).

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse recently gelded, has been competitive in tight finishes and suits good ground conditions
runners_data.comment: 0-8; fifth of eight on Kempton return (7f; 14-1, beaten 4l) six weeks ago; 1lb lower.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8; lost out in tight finishes at Musselburgh (5f novice) and Lingfield (6f nursery) as a juvenile; gelded over the winter and fifth of eight on Kempton return (7f; 14-1, beaten 4l) six weeks ago; 1lb lower but likely needs a fraction more.

runners_data.name: Vencedora
runners_data.note: Natural leader back quickly after 10 days, made all to win last time and will want to dictate again
runners_data.comment: Newcastle novice winner (6f); possibly needed comeback run at Southwell (7f) ten days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped well on Haydock debut (third) and off the mark next time in a modest three-runner Newcastle novice (6f; 2-1; made all); possibly needed her recent comeback run at Southwell (7f; fifth of seven), and dropping back in trip looks sensible; chance, despite a poor draw.

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 200-day winter break, previously consistent and now gelded for this comeback
runners_data.comment: Scrambled home in 5f novice at Leicester (6-5 fav) last October; gelded; back from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Rewarded for a series of consistent efforts when scrambling home in a 5f novice at Leicester (6-5 favourite) last October; gelded, and back from a winter break with the possibility of more to come; shouldn't be troubled by returning to 6f.

runners_data.name: Siouxpersonic
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer back after 210 days, has winning form but returning to new trainer after stable switch
runners_data.comment: 5f Southwell winner for Ed Bethell; sold for 40,000gns; returns to 6f for stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: With Ed Bethell when knuckling down to land the odds in a 5f fillies' maiden at Southwell (runner-up 2-3 since) last September; joined this trainer the following month for 40,000gns; is fairly weighted back over 6f in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Solar Cooper
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who hung left-handed on recent stable debut, significant drop in grade may help
runners_data.comment: Hung left-handed and dropped out accordingly on recent stable debut at Beverley (7.5f).
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to progress for Brian Ellison (0-4; 5f-6f); hung left-handed and dropped out accordingly on recent stable debut at Beverley (7.5f; 13-2, eighth of ten); may draw benefit from that comeback run but others make way more appeal.

runners_data.name: Liverpool Star
runners_data.note: Yet to win in 10 attempts but consistently places, does best work late and suits this trip
runners_data.comment: Bumped at the start but recovered to do solid late work at Catterick (5f) latest; 6f fine.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win (0-10), going closest when beaten a head at Newcastle (6f nursery) in December; bumped at the start but recovered to do solid late work at Catterick (5f, good; third of ten, beaten 1l) 17 days ago; same mark (holds Contorno) for return to 6f.

runners_data.name: Contorno
runners_data.note: Maintains unbeaten Newcastle record over 5f but weakened when stepped up to 6f last time
runners_data.comment: No excuses when a weakening fifth (Liverpool Star third) on turf return at Catterick (5f).
runners_data.spotlight: Dictated a steady pace to maintain his unbeaten Newcastle record (5f; 2-2) on penultimate start; no excuses when a weakening fifth (Liverpool Star third) on turf return at Catterick (5f, good; 6-1) 17 days ago; 2lb above last winning mark (AW).

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 201 days with first-time tongue tie, showed some improvement in handicaps
runners_data.comment: Closer when fifth on handicap debut at Pontefract (6f; first-time tongue-tie) last October
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't offer much initially, but did at least get closer to the principals when fifth of ten on handicap debut at Pontefract (6f, nursery; soft; in a first-time tongue-tie) last October; hasn't that many miles on the clock but does lack a recent run; others preferred.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Nguru and Vencedora are both confirmed front runners who will contest the early pace from the off, with Arishka's Dream, Koffee And Kale and Contorno also likely to be prominent early. This sets up an honest gallop over 6f with genuine pace throughout, as neither leader will want to concede an advantage. The strong early pace will stretch the field and create opportunities for those with tactical speed who can track the pace without getting involved in the early battle. This race shape strongly favors prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can sit just off the pace, rather than pure hold-up horses who may find too much to do.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest pace setup
scenarios.trigger: If both Blue Nguru and Vencedora go forward as expected and maintain a solid gallop
scenarios.body: The genuine pace will stretch the field and set up perfectly for those sitting prominently behind the leaders. Horses like Arishka's Dream and Liverpool Star can track the pace and strike in the final furlong when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets an uncontested lead and the pace becomes more sedate
scenarios.body: Either Blue Nguru or Vencedora could steal a march and prove hard to peg back over this sharp 6f trip. The lack of early pressure would allow them to dictate terms and kick clear when it matters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders go too hard and tie up badly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The sustained pace battle between Blue Nguru and Vencedora could set it up perfectly for closers with a turn of foot. Hold-up horses like Siouxpersonic and Ecclefechan would benefit from the strong gallop ahead of them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical speed wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more moderate than expected and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Horses with natural speed who haven't been committed early could time their run perfectly. This would suit those who can quicken off a steady pace rather than pure front runners or hold-up specialists.

watchPoints.text: Blue Nguru and Vencedora could go too fast early if both determined to lead, compromising each other's chances
Koffee And Kale returning after 200 days off may need the run despite his previous consistency
Solar Cooper's tendency to hang left-handed could be problematic if repeating that behavior here
Siouxpersonic switching trainers after 210-day break creates uncertainty about current form and fitness
Contorno's pace-setting tactics worked over 5f but may be found out over this extra furlong
